existing_claims_assessment.result: No contradiction or unsupported attribution identified between the 12 bounded paraphrases and the source contexts read. Existing limitations must carry into Q&A. This does not promote every context paragraph into an approved claim.
concrete_attribution_controls: 1989 and 1996 letters are authored by Buffett; reported statements about Charlie remain Buffett narration, not direct Munger quotations.
The high-index-price/Japan warning in 2002 is Munger’s; Buffett then discusses alternatives. Do not merge those turns into a single Buffett statement.
The distinction between professing and having integrity in 2010 is Munger’s. Buffett discusses peer pressure and Berkshire budgeting; Munger then discusses consequences.
The audience question’s claimed three-key-question framework is a questioner premise, not established as Buffett or Munger’s own framework by this exchange.

questions.suggested_question: Can a wonderful company be a poor investment?
questions.answer_supported: Yes: Buffett treats business economics and purchase price as distinct conditions. A bargain in a weak business may erode with continued ownership, while even a strong business can be bought so dearly that its value takes an extended period to catch up.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: When evaluating an individual business, keep two questions separate: are the business economics attractive, and is the purchase price sensible? A favorable answer to one does not establish the other.
practical_guidance.basis: 1989 section contrasts weak business returns with a cheap entry price, then states a preference for strong businesses at a fair price. The 1996 section explicitly warns that the best businesses can be overpriced.
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: People who choose to evaluate individual businesses; this is an assessment distinction, not an instruction to buy a particular security.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: A numerical valuation formula, universal discount, target return, or current buy/wait/sell decision.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: Do not let admiration for management substitute for examining the business economics. Buffett’s examples include able, honest managers whose businesses still had poor economics.
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: The examples concern Berkshire textile operations and Hochschild Kohn; they establish a distinction, not a conclusion about any current manager or company.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: A claim that capable managers never improve a business, or that all distressed/cheap businesses are bad investments.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: If you choose individual stocks, assess businesses within what you can evaluate and recognize the boundary of that ability.
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: The 1996 letter first recommends low-cost indexing for most investors; its stock-selection discussion is conditional on choosing to build a portfolio.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: A general recommendation that everyone stock-pick or concentrate a portfolio.

critical_limits: 1989 is the report year; the letter is signed March 2, 1990. 1996 is the report year; the letter is signed February 28, 1997. First publication dates are not established here.
The 1996 warning that market overpayment risk might then be high describes that historical moment. It is not evidence that today’s market or any present security is overpriced.
The 1989 cheap-business criticism preserves the liquidator/quick-resale distinction. Its numerical example must not become a required holding period or return threshold.
Do not claim that holding indefinitely guarantees recovery from overpayment. The 1996 wording warns of an extended catch-up period, not guaranteed recovery.
The source does not supply a fair-value formula or objective test that a company is wonderful. Acknowledge that unresolved evaluation task.
Pair the 1989 quality preference with the 1996 price qualification as a thematic synthesis; do not claim a formal revision or newly discovered evolution.
unsupported_extensions_to_reject: Use a particular P/E ratio or discount percentage as Buffett’s purchase rule.
Current companies named in historical examples are recommended purchases today.
Strong or honest management makes poor business economics harmless.

questions.suggested_question: Is honest management enough—and how do incentives matter?
questions.alternative_user_question: How can I judge whether management is trustworthy?
questions.answer_boundary: The reviewed sources offer a way to think about the problem, not a reliable test of personal honesty. They distinguish admirable people, sound business economics and organizational pressures.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: Treat a declaration of integrity as a claim, not proof. Munger explicitly says it is difficult to know whether professing integrity means possessing it.
practical_guidance.speaker: Charlie Munger
practical_guidance.must_not_add: An invented checklist, personality score, interview technique or guarantee for detecting dishonesty.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: Look at the pressures around a decision as well as the person. Buffett describes reducing situations that can tempt managers to manipulate reported results.
practical_guidance.speaker: Warren Buffett
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: A question to ask when examining or designing reporting arrangements; the concrete example is budgets submitted to Berkshire headquarters, not a universal governance prescription.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: Abolish budgets, forecasting, targets or all performance-linked compensation. Buffett expressly says subsidiaries may use budgets and many do.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: Ask who bears the consequences of the decisions being made. Munger presents that connection as a response to systems that allow people to pass responsibility along.
practical_guidance.speaker: Charlie Munger
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: Munger’s interpretation of incentives during the financial crisis. This is a question about responsibility, not proof that one incentive mechanism always works.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: A minimum management shareholding, compensation percentage, clawback formula or legal/regulatory requirement.

practical_guidance.suggested_wording: Evaluate the people and the business separately. Buffett says he prefers people he likes, trusts and admires, while warning that this alone does not ensure business success.
practical_guidance.speaker: Warren Buffett
practical_guidance.audience_and_conditions: His 1989 retrospective on business ownership and investment mistakes. Liking someone does not itself establish trustworthiness.
practical_guidance.must_not_add: Likeability is a validated integrity test, or admirable people guarantee profitable investment outcomes.

critical_limits: If the title asks how to detect honesty, explicitly answer that these sources do not offer a foolproof detection method. A title centered on incentives and business quality better fits the evidence.
Preserve Munger’s authorship of both the integrity-declaration caution and the consequences principle. Buffett’s separate remarks must not be used to relabel those as his quotations.

The 2010 discussion responds to a question about management integrity following the financial crisis. Historical examples and numbers are the speakers’ accounts, not independently established findings of this pilot.

Do not turn Buffett’s Berkshire-headquarters budgeting example into advice to remove budgets from other organizations. He explicitly allows subsidiaries to use them and acknowledges Berkshire is not perfect.
Munger says misconduct can arise from poor cognition and self-justification, not only greed or malevolence. Avoid presenting the passage as a way to identify bad people from one observed incentive.
No invented fraud-detection checklist, due-diligence workflow, governance mechanism, remuneration design or legal advice is supported by this small evidence set.
unsupported_extensions_to_reject: Anyone who talks about integrity is dishonest.
Managers who own shares are necessarily trustworthy.
Good people guarantee good investment results.
A historical mortgage-system criticism proves a current individual or firm is unethical.

practical_section_label_recommendation: Use Source-supported implications or Questions these passages support. Mark the questions as editorial applications rather than a checklist dictated by Buffett.
final_review_required: Check the actual Q&A wording, citations, audience, date qualifiers and source boundaries after drafting. No draft answer is approved by this pre-draft audit.
